+title: ".clineignore (deprecated)"

 <Warning>
-  **`.clineignore` will be deprecated soon.**
+  **Cline no longer reads `.clineignore` on its own.**
 
-  `.clineignore` filters what Cline loads automatically, but it is not a security or access-control boundary — ignored files can still be read via explicit `@` mentions or shell commands. We're moving away from it as a supported feature.
+  The VS Code extension stopped applying `.clineignore` in version 4.0, and the CLI and Cline Desktop never applied it. A `.clineignore` file now does nothing unless you add the hook below. See [Deprecations](/resources/deprecations#clineignore).

Let's remove this documentation entirely now that .clineignore is no longer supported anywhere.

I think we should remove the filter as well, because it isn't effective: The model can just `cat` these files and read them anyway.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
In cases like this, I would rather clean up the product and delete the line from the documentation. Or fix the product and keep it.

Reason is, it looks silly to document something that does nothing. Why did we document this thing that does nothing, and not other things?

It would be different if we indicated it does X, caveat, it is broken right now. That implies it WILL do that thing again soon...

TBH if something was broken enough for us not to notice for a long time, and isn't a core part of the product, it is probably a good sign we should remove it. I am OK if you nominate some PRs you want fixed in a certain direction and block landing the doc update on those PRs resolving. Only exception is cases where that's a ton of complicated work, in that case, we have to keep moving forward and we should document the caveats and fix them asynchronously. This is presumably not that scale of issue.)

-Manage MCP servers. See [MCP](/mcp/mcp-overview).
+Manage MCP servers. In a terminal, `cline mcp` opens a menu to list, add, edit, enable or disable, authorize and delete servers. See [MCP](/mcp/mcp-overview).
 
 ```bash

+cline mcp add files --yes -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem .
 ```

-```bash

+`cline mcp add` (or `install`) saves a server: a command and its arguments after `--` for a local server, or a URL for a remote one. Without `--yes`, it opens the add wizard with those fields filled in. `cline mcp remove` (or `uninstall`) deletes a server by name.
 
 ### `doctor`
 
 Diagnose and fix configuration issues.
 
 ```bash
 cline doctor
+cline doctor fix    # Kill all running Cline processes
+cline doctor log    # Open the CLI log file
 ```
 
 ### `history|h [options]`
 
-List session history or manage saved sessions.
+List session history or manage saved sessions. In a terminal, `cline history` opens a session picker; otherwise it prints the list.
 
 ```bash
 cline history
-cline h
+cline history --json --limit 10
+cline history export <session-id> -o session.html
+cline history delete --session-id <session-id>
 ```
 
+| Option or command | Description |
+|--------|-------------|
+| `--json` | Print the sessions as JSON |
+| `--limit <count>` | Maximum number of sessions to show (default: `50`) |
+| `--page <number>` | Page of results to show |

## JSON Output Format
 
-When using `--json`, each message is a JSON object on its own line:
+With `--json`, the CLI prints one JSON object per line. Every line has a `type` and a `ts` (an ISO 8601 timestamp):
 
 ```json
-{"type": "say", "text": "I'll create the file now.", "ts": 1760501486669, "say": "text"}
+{"ts":"2026-10-07T04:49:43.041Z","type":"agent_event","event":{"type":"done","reason":"completed","text":"Hello!","iterations":1}}
 ```
 
-| Field | Type | Description |
-|-------|------|-------------|
-| `type` | `"ask"` or `"say"` | Message category |
-| `text` | `string` | Message content |
-| `ts` | `number` | Unix timestamp in milliseconds |
-| `say` | `string` | Subtype when `type` is `"say"` |
-| `ask` | `string` | Subtype when `type` is `"ask"` |
-| `reasoning` | `string` | Model reasoning (if available) |
-| `partial` | `boolean` | `true` while streaming |
+| `type` | Description |
+|--------|-------------|
+| `agent_event` | An event from the agent, in `event`. `event.type` is one of the [agent events](/sdk/reference/events#agentevent): `content_start`, `content_update`, `content_end`, `iteration_start`, `iteration_end`, `usage`, `notice`, `done` or `error` |
+| `hook_event` | A lifecycle hook ran (`hookEventName`, `agentId`, `taskId`) |
+| `team_event` | An event from an [agent team](/cli/agent-teams), in `event` |
+| `run_result` | The run finished: `finishReason`, `iterations`, `usage`, `durationMs`, `model` and the final `text` |
+| `run_aborted` | Follows `run_result` when the run was stopped (`reason`, `message`) |

+### `skill [args...]`
+
+Manage skills through the open [skills CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/skills) (`npx skills`). `add` and `remove` install into Cline unless you pass your own `--agent`. See [Skills](/customization/skills).

 ### `hub`
 
-Manage the local hub daemon.
+Manage the local hub daemon. The hub starts automatically when Cline needs it.
+
+```bash
+cline hub status     # Show whether the hub is running
+cline hub ensure     # Start the hub if it isn't running and print its URL
+cline hub start      # Same as ensure
+cline hub stop       # Stop the hub and the sessions running in it
+cline hub drain      # Refuse new work while accepted runs finish (--off lifts it)
+cline hub upgrade    # Drain, wait for the hub to go idle, then restart it
